title: Distributions
intro: A small number of distributions describe a large share of the randomness met in practice. Each arises from a simple mechanism, and the mechanisms connect them into one family tree.

blocks.text: Learn each distribution by the story that produces it, not by its formula: the binomial counts successes in independent trials, the Poisson counts rare events, the exponential waits for the next one, the normal is what sums of many small effects look like. The formulas then follow, and so do the relationships between them.

items: Bernoulli, Binomial and Geometric (#/probability/distributions/binomial-and-geometric): independent trials and what to count about them.
The Poisson Distribution (#/probability/distributions/poisson): rare events, the law of small numbers.
Exponential and Gamma (#/probability/distributions/exponential-and-gamma): waiting times and memorylessness.
The Normal Distribution (#/probability/distributions/normal): the bell curve, standardisation and its tails.
Sampling Distributions (#/probability/distributions/sampling-distributions): chi-square, Student's t, F and beta, the distributions that statistics produces.

blocks.alt: Boxes for Bernoulli, Binomial, Geometric, Poisson, Exponential, Gamma, Normal, Chi-square and Student t joined by labelled arrows: Bernoulli sums to binomial and waiting gives geometric; binomial tends to Poisson and, by the CLT, to normal; Poisson gaps are exponential; exponentials sum to gamma; squared normals sum to chi-square, which is a gamma; a normal over the root of a chi-square gives t.
blocks.caption: How the standard distributions arise from one another.
